A structure found in the red pulp of the spleen between the sinusoids, consisting of fibrils and connective tissue cells with a large population of monocytes and macrophages. These cords contain half of the human body's monocytes as a reserve so that after tissue injury these monocytes can move in and aid locally sourced monocytes in wound healing. Erythrocytes pass through the cords of Billroth before entering the sinusoids. The passage into the sinusoids may be seen as a bottleneck, where erythrocytes need to be flexible in order to pass through. In disorders of erythrocyte shape and/or flexibility, such as hereditary spherocytosis, erythrocytes fail to pass through and get phagocytosed, causing extravascular hemolysis.
definition.es: Estructura que se encuentra en la pulpa roja del bazo entre los sinusoides, formada por fibrillas y células de tejido conjuntivo con una gran población de monocitos y macrófagos. Estos cordones contienen la mitad de los monocitos del cuerpo humano como reserva, de modo que, tras una lesión tisular, estos monocitos pueden desplazarse y ayudar a los monocitos de origen local en la cicatrización de las heridas. Los eritrocitos atraviesan los cordones de Billroth antes de entrar en los sinusoides. El paso hacia los sinusoides puede considerarse un cuello de botella, en el que los eritrocitos deben ser flexibles para poder atravesarlo. En los trastornos de la forma o de la flexibilidad de los eritrocitos, como la esferocitosis hereditaria, los eritrocitos no logran atravesarlo y son fagocitados, lo que provoca hemólisis extravascular.

The Medial forebrain bundle (MFB), is a complex bundle of axons coming from the basal olfactory regions, the periamygdaloid region, and the septal nuclei, and passing to the lateral hypothalamus, with some carrying on into the tegmentum. It contains both ascending and descending fibers. It also represents a part of the mesolimbic pathway, carrying information between the ventral tegmentum and the nucleus accumbens. It is commonly accepted that the MFB is a part of the reward system, involved in the integration of reward and pleasure. Electrical stimulation of the medial forebrain bundle is believed to cause sensations of pleasure. This hypothesis is based upon intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS) studies. Animals will work for MFB ICSS, and humans report that MFB ICSS is intensely pleasurable. This is most likely because the medial forebrain bundle carries information from the ventral tegmental area (VTA) to the nucleus accumbens (nAcc or Acb). The nAcc is a recognized reward center, and activation of the pathway from the VTA to the nAcc is believed to be rewarding, which is why it is sometimes referred to as the hedonic highway. [WP,unvetted].

A complex network of nerves located in the abdomen behind the stomach. The celiac plexus is located near where the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, and renal arteries branch from the abdominal aorta. It is behind the stomach and the omental bursa and in front of the crura of the diaphragm, on the level of the first lumbar vertebra, L1. The plexus is formed (in part) by the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves of both sides, and also parts of the right vagus nerve. The celiac plexus proper consists of the celiac ganglia with a network of interconnecting fibers. The aorticorenal ganglia are often considered to be part of the celiac ganglia, and thus, part of the plexus. [WP,unvetted].
definition.es: Red compleja de nervios situada en el abdomen, detrás del estómago. El plexo celíaco se encuentra cerca del lugar donde el tronco celíaco, la arteria mesentérica superior y las arterias renales se ramifican desde la aorta abdominal. Está detrás del estómago y de la bolsa omental y delante de los pilares del diafragma, a la altura de la primera vértebra lumbar, L1. El plexo está formado (en parte) por los nervios esplácnicos mayor y menor de ambos lados, y también por partes del nervio vago derecho. El plexo celíaco propiamente dicho consta de los ganglios celíacos con una red de fibras de interconexión. Los ganglios aorticorrenales se consideran a menudo parte de los ganglios celíacos y, por tanto, parte del plexo. [WP,unvetted].

The system also includes all the structures dedicated to the circulation and production of lymphocytes, which includes the spleen, thymus, bone marrow and the lymphoid tissue associated with the digestive system[WP].

The medial dorsal nucleus (or dorsomedial nucleus of thalamus) is a large nucleus in the thalamus. It receives inputs from the Pre-Frontal Cortex and the Limbic System and in turn relays them to the Pre-Frontal Association Cortex. As a result, it plays a crucial role in attention, planning, organization, abstract thinking, multi-tasking and active memory. The connections of the medial dorsal nucleus have even been used to delineate the prefrontal cortex of the Göttingen minipig brain. By stereology the number of brain cells in the region has been estimated to around 6.43 million neurons in the adult human brain and 36.3 million glial cells, and with the newborn having quite different numbers: around 11.2 million neurons and 10.6 million glial cells. Lesions of the medial dorsal nucleus have been associated with Wernicke's encephalopathy [WP,unvetted].

definition.en: In the circulatory system of animals, a portal venous system occurs when a capillary bed drains into another capillary bed through veins, without first going through the heart. Both capillary beds and the blood vessels that connect them are considered part of the portal venous system. They are relatively uncommon as the majority of capillary beds drain into veins which then drain into the heart, not into another capillary bed. Portal venous systems are considered venous because the blood vessels that join the two capillary beds are either veins or venules. Examples of such systems include the hepatic portal system and the hypophyseal portal system. Unqualified, 'portal venous system' often refers to the hepatic portal system. For this reason, 'portal vein' most commonly refers to the hepatic portal vein[WP].

definition.en: The superficial palmar arch is formed predominantly by the ulnar artery, with a contribution from the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery. However, in some individuals the contribution from the radial artery might be absent, and instead anastomoses with either the princeps pollicis artery, the radialis indicis artery, or the median artery, the former two of which are branches from the radial artery. Alternative names for this arterial arch are: superficial volar arch, superficial ulnar arch, arcus palmaris superficialis, or arcus volaris superficialis. The arch passes across the palm in a curve with its convexity downward. If one were to fully extend the thumb, the superficial palmar arch would lie approximately at the level of a line drawn from the distal border of the thumb across the palm. The superficial palmar arch is more distal than the deep palmar arch. Three common palmar digital arteries arise from the arch, proceeding down on the second, third, and fourth lumbrical muscles, respectively. They each receive a contribution from a palmar metacarpal artery. Near the level of the metacarpophalangeal joints, each common palmar digital artery divides into two proper palmar digital arteries.

UBERON:0007260.labelEs: disco intervertebral de la tercera vértebra cervical

definition.en: An intervertebral disk that connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 3 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 4.
definition.es: Disco intervertebral que conecta una tercera vértebra cervical de mamífero con una cuarta vértebra cervical de mamífero.

definition.en: A duct that collects and carries secretions of the exocrine pancreas to the intestine.
A nucleus of brain that is part of a pontine reticular formation.

Stratified columnar epithelia is a rare type of epithelial tissue composed of column shaped cells arranged in multiple layers. Stratified columnar epithelia are found in the ocular conjunctiva of the eye, in parts of the pharynx and anus, the female's uterus, the male urethra and vas deferens. Also found in intralobular ducts in salivary glands.[WP].
An anatomical structure that connects two structures.

synonymsEn: interphalangeal joint of pedal digit II
interphalangeal joint of second digit of foot

definition.en: An interphalangeal joint of pes that is part of a pedal digit 2.
Mesentery that is located in the peritoneum.
definition.es: Mesenterio que se localiza en el peritoneo.

synonymsEn: dorsal white commissure of spinal cord
posterior white commissure of spinal cord

definition.en: A short vessel of large caliber which arises from the internal pudendal between the two layers of fascia of the urogenital diaphragm; it passes medialward, pierces the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm, and gives off branches which ramify in the bulb of the urethra and in the posterior part of the corpus spongiosum. It gives off a small branch to the bulbo-urethral gland.
The external junctural region between the lower part of the abdomen and the thigh.
An intestinal villus in the duodenum.
A transverse foramen that is part of a vertebral bone 2.
definition.es: Agujero transverso que forma parte de la vértebra 2.

definition.en: A muscle that arises from the spinous processes of the third to the sixth thoracic vertebrae and inserts into the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the upper two or three cervical vertebrae[WP,modified].
definition.es: Músculo que se origina en las apófisis espinosas de la tercera a la sexta vértebras torácicas y se inserta en los tubérculos posteriores de las apófisis transversas de las dos o tres vértebras cervicales superiores[WP,modified].

definition.en: Facial muscle attached to the modiolus, corner (angle) of the mouth, and zygomatic bone. See Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al.., 2011., also DuBrul, 1980.
definition.es: Músculo facial fijado al modiolo, a la comisura (ángulo) de la boca y al hueso cigomático. Véase Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al., 2011; también DuBrul, 1980.

definition.en: The smooth muscle layer of the stomach wall that functions to churn and mix food and gastric secretions as well as to move food along the digestive tract to the intestines.

UBERON:0009572.labelEs: luz del conducto central de la médula espinal
synonymsEn: cavity of central canal of spinal cord

definition.en: A cerebrospinal fluid-filled space that runs longitudinally through the length of the entire spinal cord. The central canal is contiguous with the ventricular system of the brain. The central canal represents the adult remainder of the neural tube.
definition.es: Espacio lleno de líquido cefalorraquídeo que recorre longitudinalmente toda la longitud de la médula espinal. El conducto central es continuo con el sistema ventricular del encéfalo. El conducto central representa el remanente adulto del tubo neural.

definition.en: An epithelium that is part of a vermiform appendix.
Any endocardium that is part of the right ventricle of the heart.
definition.es: Cualquier endocardio que forma parte del ventrículo derecho del corazón.

definition.en: An inter-phalangeal joint that connects a proximal phalanx to either a medial or distal phalanx.

The collection of hair that grows on the chin, cheeks and neck of human beings. Usually, only pubescent or adult males are able to grow beards. However, women with hirsutism may develop a beard. When differentiating between upper and lower facial hair, a beard specifically includes the moustache, which refers to hair above the upper lip and around it.
definition.es: Conjunto de pelo que crece en el mentón, las mejillas y el cuello de los seres humanos. Por lo general, solo los varones púberes o adultos pueden dejarse crecer la barba. Sin embargo, las mujeres con hirsutismo pueden desarrollar barba. Al diferenciar entre el vello facial superior y el inferior, la barba incluye específicamente el bigote, que se refiere al pelo situado por encima del labio superior y a su alrededor.

definition.en: A pupil that is part of a right eye.
definition.es: Pupila que forma parte de un ojo derecho.

definition.en: The space formed by the junction of the bulbar and palpebral portions of the conjunctiva, that of the upper lid being the superior conjunctival fornix (fornix conjunctivae superior) and that of the lower lid, the inferior conjunctival fornix (fornix conjunctivae inferior); the fornix is loose and flexible, allowing the free movement of the lids and eyeball.
definition.es: Espacio formado por la unión de las porciones bulbar y palpebral de la conjuntiva; el del párpado superior es el fórnix conjuntival superior (fornix conjunctivae superior) y el del párpado inferior, el fórnix conjuntival inferior (fornix conjunctivae inferior); el fórnix es laxo y flexible, lo que permite el libre movimiento de los párpados y del globo ocular.

synonymsEn: uncinate process of the ethmoid bone

definition.en: In the ethmoid bone, a curved lamina, the uncinate process, projects downward and backward from this part of the labyrinth; it forms a small part of the medial wall of the maxillary sinus, and articulates with the ethmoidal process of the inferior nasal concha.
definition.es: En el hueso etmoides, una lámina curva, la apófisis unciforme, se proyecta hacia abajo y hacia atrás desde esta parte del laberinto; forma una pequeña parte de la pared medial del seno maxilar y se articula con la apófisis etmoidal de la concha nasal inferior.

definition.en: The angular artery is the terminal part of the facial artery; it ascends to the medial angle of the eye's orbit, imbedded in the fibers of the angular head of the Quadratus labii superioris, and accompanied by the angular vein.
A lymphoid follicle containing naive B cells.
Limb segment that consists of the long bones of the pes. The metatarsals are analogous to the metacarpal bones of the manus.
The collection of all skeletal elements in an forelimb zeugopod region.
Origin: spines of upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae; insertion: occipital bone; innervation: spinal nerves; action, extends head.
A hinge joint between the head of the radius and the capitulum of the humerus.
Subdivision of the skeletal system which consists of the axial skeleton plus associated joints.

Small, mucous accessory lacrimal glands that are found underneath the eyelid where the upper and lower conjuctivae meet. Their ducts unite into a rather long sinus which open into the fornix conjunctiva. There are approximately forty Krause glands in the region of the upper eyelid, and around 6 to 8 in the region of the lower lid. The function of these glands are to produce tears which are secreted onto the surface of the conjuctiva.
definition.es: Pequeñas glándulas lagrimales accesorias mucosas que se encuentran bajo el párpado, donde se unen las conjuntivas superior e inferior. Sus conductos se unen en un seno bastante largo que se abre en el fórnix conjuntival. Hay aproximadamente cuarenta glándulas de Krause en la región del párpado superior y unas 6 a 8 en la región del párpado inferior. La función de estas glándulas es producir lágrimas, que se secretan sobre la superficie de la conjuntiva.

definition.en: A nail that is part of a manual digit 2.
A gingiva that is part of a upper jaw region.
definition.es: Encía que forma parte de una región de la mandíbula superior.

definition.en: A zone of the frontal bone that consists of two thin triangular plates, the orbital plates, which form the vaults of the orbits, and are separated from one another by a median gap, the ethmoidal notch.
definition.es: Zona del hueso frontal que consta de dos láminas delgadas y triangulares, las láminas orbitarias, que forman las bóvedas de las órbitas y están separadas entre sí por un espacio medio, la escotadura etmoidal.

definition.en: An acinus that is part of a salivary gland.
The supratrochlear artery (or frontal artery), one of the terminal branches of the ophthalmic artery, branches off where the ophthalmic travels posterior to the trochlea.
Epithelium that derives from the mesoderm. [Automatically generated definition].
The lymphocytic cell population present in the mucosa of the nasopharyngeal duct of some animals.
The segment of the pes that is distal to the metatarsal region and consists of the pedal digits (toes).
Brodmann area 8 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in planning complex movements.
Brodmann area 22 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in auditory processing.

The posterior border of the ala, shorter than the anterior, also presents two projections separated by a notch, the posterior superior iliac spine and the posterior inferior iliac spine. The posterior inferior iliac spine corresponds with the posterior extremity of the auricular surface.
definition.es: El borde posterior del ala, más corto que el anterior, presenta también dos salientes separados por una escotadura, la espina ilíaca posterosuperior y la espina ilíaca posteroinferior. La espina ilíaca posteroinferior corresponde al extremo posterior de la superficie auricular.

definition.en: A muscular coat that is part of a ileum.

synonymsEn: stratum radiatum of the CA3 field

definition.en: Part of stratum radiatum in area CA3, lying superficial to the stratum lucidum and deep to CA3 stratum lacunosum-moleculare.

UBERON:0015717.labelEn: smooth muscle tissue layer of ejaculatory duct

definition.en: A smooth muscle tissue that is part of a ejaculatory duct.

The retropharyngeal lymph nodes, from one to three in number, lie in the buccopharyngeal fascia, behind the upper part of the pharynx and in front of the arch of the atlas, being separated, however, from the latter by the Longus capitis. Their afferents drain the nasal cavities, the nasal part of the pharynx, and the auditory tubes. Their efferents pass to the superior deep cervical glands. They are in the retropharyngeal space.
definition.es: Los nódulos linfáticos retrofaríngeos, de uno a tres, se sitúan en la fascia bucofaríngea, por detrás de la parte superior de la faringe y por delante del arco del atlas, del que están separados, no obstante, por el largo de la cabeza. Sus aferentes drenan las cavidades nasales, la porción nasal de la faringe y las trompas auditivas. Sus eferentes se dirigen a los ganglios cervicales profundos superiores. Se encuentran en el espacio retrofaríngeo.

definition.en: One of the lymph nodes that form a chain around the ileocolic artery.
The line of junction between the horizontal parts of the palatine bones that extends from both sides of the skull to form the posterior part of the hard palate.
definition.es: Línea de unión entre las láminas horizontales de los huesos palatinos que se extiende desde ambos lados del cráneo para formar la parte posterior del paladar duro.

synonymsEn: posterior part of fornix of vagina

definition.en: The vaginal fornix that is behind the cervix. It is close to the recto-uterine pouch.
Luminal space of the left ventricle of the heart.
definition.es: Espacio luminal del ventrículo izquierdo del corazón.

definition.en: A vermilion that is part of a upper lip.
definition.es: Bermellón que forma parte de un labio superior.

synonymsEn: triangular ridge of crown of tooth

definition.en: Endocardium that is part of the left atrium.
definition.es: Endocardio que forma parte del atrio izquierdo.

synonymsEn: ventral median fissure of spinal cord

definition.en: A fissure in the midline of the anterior surface of the spinal cord.
The portion of the peripharyngeal space limited by the lateral wall of the pharynx, the cervical vertebrae and medial pterygoid muscle.

synonymsEn: auricularis posterior branch of facial nerve

definition.en: A branch of the facial nerve that innervates the posterior auricular and intrinsic muscles of the auricle and, through its occipital branch, innervates the occipital belly of the occipitofrontal muscle.
definition.es: Ramo del nervio facial que inerva los músculos auricular posterior e intrínsecos de la oreja y, a través de su ramo occipital, inerva el vientre occipital del músculo occipitofrontal.

definition.en: A muscle layer that is part of the sigmoid colon.
A dense surrounding coat of white fibers, as the sheath of the inferior olive and of the dentate nucleus.

Capillary that has endothelial cells that provide an uninterrupted lining, and only allow small molecules, like water and ions to diffuse through tight junctions which leave gaps of unjoined membrane which are called intercellular clefts.
An ethmoidal vein that accompanies a posterior ethmoidal artery. The posterior ethmoidal vein often drains into a venous network under the orbital roof.
definition.es: Vena etmoidal que acompaña a una arteria etmoidal posterior. La vena etmoidal posterior drena a menudo en una red venosa situada bajo el techo de la órbita.

definition.en: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the uterus.

A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, inferiorly and laterally towards the inferior pole of the kidney. It supplies the inferior lobe of the kidney, which encompasses the whole of the inferior pole of the kidney, including the anterior and posterior surfaces.
definition.es: Arteria segmentaria renal que pasa por delante de la pelvis renal, en dirección inferior y lateral hacia el polo inferior del riñón. Irriga el lóbulo inferior del riñón, que abarca la totalidad del polo inferior del riñón, incluidas las caras anterior y posterior.

UBERON:8920022.labelEs: arteria de la cola del páncreas

definition.en: An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the tail of the pancreas.
definition.es: Arteria que se ramifica de la arteria esplénica e irriga la cola del páncreas.

UBERON:8930070.labelEn: muscle layer of fallopian tube isthmus
UBERON:8930070.labelEs: capa muscular del istmo de la trompa uterina

definition.en: A muscular coat that is part of the isthmus of the fallopian tube, consisting of outer longitudinal and inner circular layers of smooth muscle that are responsible for peristaltic contractions propelling the ovum toward the uterus.
definition.es: Túnica muscular que forma parte del istmo de la trompa uterina, constituida por capas externa longitudinal e interna circular de músculo liso, responsables de las contracciones peristálticas que impulsan el óvulo hacia el útero.
